meta.title: notabot: open-source bot detection, in your own browser
meta.description: See everything your browser tells a website, how notabot cross-checks it for lies, and what a small AI model makes of it. One script tag, MIT, front-end only.
nav.label: Sections
passport.aria: Your browser's passport, filled in from what it told this page
passport.portrait: Your browser's canvas fingerprint: the drawing notabot hashes
passport.portraitCaption: Canvas render, as your graphics stack drew it
passport.mrz: Machine-readable zone encoding your browser's papers
border.title: Your browser is about to cross a border.
border.lede: notabot reads what your browser declares, checks it for contradictions and stamps a verdict. No puzzle unless it has doubts, and then only a slider. Open source, front-end only.
border.note: Nothing leaves this page. The AI verdict below is opt-in and uses your own model.
border.forceSlider: Show me the secondary inspection anyway
papers.title: Everything your browser told this page
papers.lede: Read without a single permission prompt, and nothing was sent anywhere. Each line says what it reveals and how much it says about you; a reading that contradicts the rest is marked in red.
report.title: The inspector's report
report.lede: One odd answer proves nothing: real people use VPNs, old laptops and privacy extensions. What gives a bot away is answers that contradict each other. Every rule below ran on your browser.
report.pending: Run the check above to file the report.
officer.title: Secondary inspection: ask an AI officer
officer.lede: The video's point: every captcha ends by sending the clues to a model that scores you. Here you pick the model and read exactly what it is sent. It only ever sees numbers, yes/no values and fixed words, never text your browser could have written, so a bot cannot talk its way in.
officer.keyHint: Kept on this device only, encrypted in IndexedDB, and sent to that provider alone.
officer.proxyHint: Your Worker or proxy holds the key; this page never does.
officer.localHint: Run OLLAMA_ORIGINS=* ollama serve so the page may call it.
officer.needCheck: Run the check at the top first: the officer needs the papers.
officer.needModel: Choose a model and fill in its key or endpoint.
officer.verdict: {model}: {verdict} at {c} % confidence, in {ms} ms. Blended with the rules: bot probability {p} %.
officer.unreadable: The model answered, but not in the requested format. Its raw answer is on the right.
officer.promptHint: The exact instructions and features, before anything is sent.
officer.promptPending: Appears once your browser has been read.
network.title: Papers a page cannot read
network.lede: Some of the strongest evidence never reaches JavaScript. Only a server can see it, which is why notabot ships a Cloudflare Worker for the day you enforce. Timestamps link to the video.
network.ip: A home internet provider or a datacentre (AWS, OVH, Hetzner), and whether its location agrees with your time zone.
network.tcp: The first SYN packet's TTL, window size and option order differ per operating system: a Windows user agent over a Linux stack gives itself away.
network.tls: Cipher suites and extensions differ between Chrome's BoringSSL, Firefox's NSS and Python's OpenSSL.
network.http: A second fingerprint of the client, layered under TLS.
network.scale: Thousands of sessions on the same path with the same timings: invisible from one browser, obvious from the server.
embed.title: Put it on your site
embed.lede: Four ways in, from one line to a server that checks every request.
embed.scriptHint: Adds the check to the form and holds back the submission until it passes. The token lands in a hidden notabot-token field.
embed.npmHint: Every module is its own entry point: notabot/signals, /score, /behavior, /pow, /llm, /server, /widget.
embed.workerHint: Signed puzzles, server-side signals, your model with your key, and a reCAPTCHA-style siteverify.
limits.title: What this cannot do
limits.forgeable: In the page alone, a verdict can be forged: a bot can skip the script or replay a good result. Enforcement needs the server half (the Worker), which checks the proof of work and signs the token.
limits.privacy: Privacy tools (Brave, Firefox's fingerprinting protection, canvas blockers) change some readings. They count as weak evidence, never as a verdict on their own.
limits.model: The AI officer gives a second opinion. A decisive rule, such as navigator.webdriver, is never argued away by it.
limits.access: The slider works with the keyboard and the behaviour checks never block alone. Offer another way through for people who need it.
footer.video: “En vrai, les captchas… c'est encore utile ?” by V2F for overfl0w
embed.middlewareHint: Validates the request itself (headers a browser always sends, client hints, HTTP libraries, protocol, network) and the token: signed, bound to its browser and IP, used once. Express, Hono, or any Fetch server (Next.js, Bun, Workers).
